key_insight: A frozen, general-purpose LLM can generate promising quantum circuit parameters for structured Hamiltonians, but performs worse than Adam optimization on general random Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: LLM-generated circuit parameters enable independently verifiable energy evaluations, offering a safer interface than trusting direct LLM energy predictions.
method: Generate complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions.
Optionally refine parameters using iterative energy feedback and compare against Adam optimization.
Test blind circuit interpretation through algorithm identification and measurement-outcome prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluation spans general random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, and molecular systems; feedback generally yields limited improvement, while direct energy predictions can violate spectral lower bounds.
watch_item: Performance depends on problem structure; generated parameters require independent energy evaluation and should not be assumed to replace conventional optimization.
paper_title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
